item.title: Why Prosecutors May Face Legal Hurdles in the Cornell Investigation
item.description: Experts in sexual assault cases said it may not be easy to win a conviction on the rape allegations that Jane Doe has made against fraternity members.
item.dc:creator: Santul Nerkar and Benjamin Weiser
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cornell University has been rocked by accusations that seven male students sexually assaulted a woman.

item.title: How The New York Times Is Reporting on the Cornell Rape Investigation
item.description: Times editors explore the thinking behind our coverage of the explosive allegations that have roiled a campus and the country.
item.dc:creator: Megan DiTrolio, Mike Abrams, Nikita Stewart, Sarah Garland and Susan Wessling
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Sexual assault allegations have rocked Cornell’s campus and put the university under a spotlight.

item.title: Soft Jobs Report Boosts Market Bets Fed Will Skip October Rate Increase
item.description: The odds of an interest rate change at the Federal Reserve’s meeting in late October have dropped following a softer jobs report and strong signaling from bank officials.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.category: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
item.media:description: John C. Williams, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, in 2025. He said this week that there was “no need for urgency” in the wake of September’s increase.

item.title: The Powerful Yet Fragile Force Propping Up Stocks and the Economy
item.description: The artificial intelligence boom has pushed up the stock market, even as interest rates have pulled it down, our columnist says.
item.dc:creator: Jeff Sommer

item.title: Republicans Pull Money From North Carolina Senate Race As Midterm Prospects Dim
item.description: As the Republicans try to hold their majority, the Senate Leadership Fund is diverting resources to Kansas, which has become a growing concern for the party.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:description: Michael Whatley, the Republican candidate for Senate in North Carolina, has consistently trailed his Democratic opponent in the polls.

item.title: Flurry of Lawsuits Shows Both Parties Preparing for Post-Election Challenges
item.description: Republicans are using the courts to hunt for noncitizen voters. Democrats worry the G.O.P. is trying make it harder for eligible voters to cast ballots — and paving the way to try to toss valid election results.
item.dc:creator: Richard Fausset
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: A voter casting a ballot at Miller Elementary School in Dearborn, Mich., during the state’s primary in August. Scores of lawsuits from the two major political parties and their allies reveal the likely battle lines for post-election challenges.

item.title: The Rich People Democrats Aren’t Talking About
item.description: As billionaires become a popular political target, a new book urges Washington not to lose sight of a much larger, and quieter, group of wealthy business owners.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Duehren

item.title: How Flydubai Passengers and Crew Averted Disaster After Pilot Was Stabbed During Flight
item.description: A badly wounded Indian pilot managed to unlock the cockpit door. Four Israeli men teamed up to overwhelm an attacker and avert disaster.
item.dc:creator: David M. Halbfinger, Natan Odenheimer, Adam Rasgon, Johnatan Reiss and Aaron Boxerman
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:description: A FlyDubai plane carrying Israeli passengers who had earlier been aboard another FlyDubai aircraft that made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia approaches Ben Gurion International Airport near Tel Aviv on Wednesday.

item.title: Indian Pilot Stabbed on FlyDubai Flight Recalls Sudden Attack
item.description: Capt. Smit Machchhar, who was stabbed by his co-pilot midair between Dubai and Tel Aviv, said he “had to act” to prevent a crash despite serious injuries.
item.dc:creator: Pragati K.B.
item.media:credit: Israel's Foreign Ministry, via Associated Press
item.media:description: Capt. Smit Machchhar in a photo released by Israel’s Foreign Ministry.

item.title: U.S. and Allies Agree to Release Diesel Reserves as Prices Soar
item.description: The Group of 7, which includes Britain, France and Japan, announced the release of 100 million barrels over four months, effective immediately.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Friedman and Rebecca F. Elliott
item.media:description: President Trump made the announcement on social media on Friday.

item.title: Truckers Are ‘Just Trying to Hang On’ When a Fill-Up Tops $1,000
item.description: Truckers are among the hardest hit by the soaring cost of diesel fuel. High prices are forcing some to stay on the road for months and others to park their rigs.
item.dc:creator: Audra D. S. Burch
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Hilary Swift for The New York Times
item.media:description: The price of diesel fuel has skyrocketed, turning a fill-up into an $1,000-a-tank ordeal.

item.title: Sales of Hulking Pickups and S.U.V.s Sag as Fuel Prices Soar
item.description: Sales of big pickup trucks and sport utility vehicles have dipped as more Americans buy hybrids and smaller cars.
item.dc:creator: Jack Ewing
item.category: Sports Utility Vehicles and Light Trucks
item.media:description: Sales of the Chevrolet Silverado were up, but the growth came from a light-duty version of the truck. Sales of heavy-duty Silverados slumped as Americans shift away from full-size pickups and S.U.V.s.

item.title: Why U.S. Diesel Is So Important to Major Trading Partners
item.description: Economies in Latin America and Europe rely on American diesel. Stopping exports could tip some countries into recession, hurting trade with the United States.
item.dc:creator: Simon Romero
item.media:description: Adjusting the price of gasoline in Pôrto Alegre, Brazil, this year.

item.title: Ukraine Reports First Combat Use of Its Own Ballistic Missile

item.dc:creator: Andrew E. Kramer
item.media:description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine trumpeted the launch of the country’s first domestically made ballistic missile.

item.title: Russia Is Planning Its Most Powerful Blow Yet to Try to Freeze Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine showed European partners what it said were intercepted Russian plans to cut off major cities from power, heat and water this winter.
item.dc:creator: Constant Méheut and Jędrzej Nowicki

item.dc:creator: Ségolène Le Stradic and Mark Landler

item.title: Trump to Name Jay Clayton to Serve as A.I. Czar
